Writing a convincing takedown of one of America’s most popular prejudices is harder still. Writing a funny novel in which complex, imperfect characters make a compelling case for one of our culture’s most maligned groups—that takes smarts and heart. Fortunately for her readers, St. James is in full possession of both.” —Meredith Maran, Washington Post An unforgettable and heartwarming book-club debut following a trans high school teacher from a small town in South Dakota who befriends the only other trans woman she knows: one of her students. Erica Skyberg is thirty-five years old, recently divorced—and trans. Not that she's told anyone yet. Mitchell, South Dakota, isn't exactly bursting with other trans women. Instead, she keeps to herself, teaching by day and directing community theater by night. That is, until Abigail Hawkes enters her orbit. Abigail is seventeen, Mitchell High’s resident political dissident and Only Trans Girl. It’s a role she plays faultlessly, albeit a little reluctantly. She's also annoyed by the idea of spending her senior year secretly guiding her English teacher through her transition. But Abigail remembers the uncertainty—and loneliness—that comes with it. Besides, Erica isn’t the only one struggling to shed the weight of others’ expectations. As their unlikely friendship evolves, it comes under the scrutiny of their community. title: 101 Woodworking Projects to Build at Home: Simple DIY Builds for Beginners Using Basic Too
description: You keep telling yourself you will start woodworking when you have a bigger shop, but the truth is you need a workbench, a few feet of wall, and a clear afternoon. Most books assume a $5000 shop, while you have a folding table in a garage that still parks a car. This book proves a small shop is a design advantage, not a limitation. With 101 projects organized by use, not difficulty, you learn by building things you actually need: cutting boards, boxes, kitchen helpers, storage, shelves, gifts, games, garden pieces, and small furniture. Each project adds 1 skill, so cutting a board teaches grain and glue up, a box teaches square, and a shelf teaches mounting into studs. Inside, you will discover: • Setting up a $150 workbench at 34 to 36 inches, plus lighting and dust habits that save every finish • The starter tool list: tape, square, 2 clamps, circular saw or jigsaw, drill, sander, glue, screws, and safety gear • Choosing pine for practice at $3 per foot, poplar for paint, and maple or walnut for boards that show grain • Board builds: edge grain cutting boards, serving trays, and cheese boards with juice grooves at 1/4 inch x 1/4 inch • Box builds: keepsake boxes, sliding lid pencil boxes, and felt lined trinket boxes with hinges that stay flush • Wall projects: floating shelves at 24 inches, peg rails, and hexagon shelves with miters cut from 1 fence setting • Small furniture: side tables, wall bookshelves, and shoe benches at 18 inches high that hold a person without racking • Batching and scrap use that turns offcuts into coasters, gifts, and market stock for $2 to $5 per item Make 1 cutting board in 3 hours, then a nailed pine box in 2 hours, and notice the 2nd box goes square in half the time. title: No Table Saw Woodworking Projects for Beginners: The Easy, Stress-Free Way to Build Useful
description: What would you build this weekend, if you knew you wouldn't ruin the wood? You've got a circular saw, a free weekend, and half a garage to clear out first. What you don't have is a table saw — and almost every woodworking book acts like that's a dealbreaker. It isn't. If you've ever stood frozen in the lumber aisle wondering which boards are warped… measured twice and still cut wrong… or followed a "plan" whose numbers didn't add up and watched a twenty-dollar board turn into scrap - this book was written for you. No Table Saw Woodworking Projects for Beginners treats you like a capable adult with a few basic tools and a small space - not like someone who's supposed to already own a full workshop. Every project is built with a circular saw, a drill, and a couple of clamps , right in a small garage or an apartment . No table saw. No noisy machines. No fear. What makes this different from every other beginner book: Exact Home Depot & Lowe's shopping lists — real board sizes, how much to buy, and how to spot boards that aren't warped. No more guessing in the aisle. Cut lists that always add up — checked against every drawing, so you never lose an expensive board to a wrong number . Genuinely no table saw — every cut is made with a circular saw and a simple guide, a jigsaw, or a handsaw. "How to fix a mistake" boxes — because everyone slips, and one wrong cut shouldn't mean starting over. Plain English, every step — every tool and term explained the first time. No jargon, no feeling stupid. Three books in one: Book 1 — The Basics: the small set of skills, tools, and safe cuts you actually need. Book 2 — The Techniques: straight cuts, curves, and rock-solid joints without expensive machines — including the DIY cutting guide you build from scrap that does the table saw's job.

title: Woodworking Projects for True Beginners: 50 Step-by-Step Builds with Exact Cut Lists, Simp
description: Want to try woodworking, but don’t know where to start? Maybe you’ve watched a few videos, searched “easy woodworking projects,” and ended up more confused than when you began. One guide tells you to buy tools you’ve never used. Another skips the basic steps. A project looks simple, but the instructions assume you already know how to measure, mark, cut, clamp, drill, sand, and finish. Before you even touch a board, you’re already wondering: What tools do I actually need? What if I cut the wood wrong? What if I waste money? What if I’m just not handy? Woodworking Projects for True Beginners was written for that moment. This book is for anyone ready to stop just thinking about woodworking and finally build something useful with their own hands. You do not need a full workshop. You do not need expensive machines. You do not need years of experience. You need a safe place to work, a few basic tools, clear instructions, and projects simple enough to finish but useful enough to feel proud of. Inside, you’ll follow the Small-Win Woodworking Method: a practical beginner path that starts with setup, safety, tools, and core skills before guiding you through 50 projects one step at a time. Instead of throwing you into complicated builds, this book slows the process down. Each project gives you one clear win, one useful skill, and one more reason to keep going. You’ll move from confusion to confidence by building real projects you can use at home, give as gifts, or proudly say, “I made that.” Inside, you’ll find: • 50 beginner-friendly projects that move from small first builds to storage, outdoor projects, gifts, family builds, and simple furniture • Exact cut lists so you know what to cut before assembling • Simple step-by-step instructions for people who do not already know wood

description: Do you dream of building your own wooden creations but don’t know where to start? Would you love to make simple, beautiful, and useful projects without needing years of experience or expensive tools? 👉 If so, this book is exactly what you’ve been looking for! Many people think woodworking is complicated—something only professional craftsmen with big workshops and specialized tools can do. title: WOODWORKING PROJECT BIBLE FOR MEN: 50 Step-by-Step Projects, Essential Tools & Joinery Ski
description: You’ve got the table saw. You’ve watched the tutorials. And that “simple weekend project” is still sitting half-finished in the garage, collecting dust next to tools you’re still a little afraid to turn on. That’s not a talent problem. It’s a guidance problem — and this book fixes it. The Woodworking Project Bible for Men is a complete, step-by-step system built for men who want to stop watching and start building, even if you’ve never cut a straight line in your life. Inside, you’ll find: 50 build-along projects across three skill tiers (18 beginner, 20 intermediate, 12 advanced), so you always know exactly what to build next. Foundation chapters covering shop safety, the tools you actually need (and the ones you don’t), how to read wood, precise measuring and marking, and the joinery that shows up in nearly every project. Clear materials lists, cut lists, and numbered steps, with the reasoning behind each one explained, not just instructions to follow blindly. Illustrations at every tricky step showing exactly what “right” looks like next to what’s “off,” so you catch mistakes before they cost you a board. Real safety call-outs for every genuine hazard, every time, not buried in a disclaimer up front. A full finishing techniques chapter plus a tool maintenance and troubleshooting guide, so your projects and your tools both last. Quick-reference charts for conversions, board-foot math, and lumber sizing. Every project builds directly on the last, so your skills and your confidence compound with each piece you finish. A first cutting board turns into a bookshelf, a bookshelf turns into a bed frame, and before long you’re the guy other people ask for help.
